sample_unit: chatbot responses (30 queries x 3 LLMs x 100 repetitions)

links.outcome: Whether chatbot direct vs. indirect responses to suicide queries matched clinician-rated risk levels
links.effect: Chatbots never answered very-high-risk queries directly, and ChatGPT and Claude answered very-low-risk queries directly 100% of the time. Intermediate risk levels were not distinguished (low, medium, high vs very low not significantly different). Claude AOR=2.01, Gemini AOR=0.09 vs ChatGPT.
links.quote: LLM-based chatbots' responses to queries aligned with experts' judgment about whether to respond to queries at the extremes of suicide risk (very low and very high), but the chatbots showed inconsistency in addressing intermediate-risk queries, underscoring the need to further refine LLMs.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of commercial LLM chatbots' direct vs. indirect responses (e.g. declining or referring to hotlines) across varying clinician-rated suicide risk levels using simulated queries, without testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
